$comment: The case list every SDK's conformance suite must exercise.
The assertion CODE cannot be shared across eight languages, but the case
LIST is data, and its absence is what let coverage drift: the four later
ports gained six hardening cases the first three never got, so MAX_DEPTH
and MAX_BIGINT_DIGITS - both justified as defences against a hostile peer -
went unasserted in Python and Go for several commits with every gate green.
Each suite READS this file at run time and fails if the run did not cover
it, so adding a case here turns every language red until it is covered,
which is the point. The evidence is produced by the case executing — a
suite cannot satisfy the check by listing names it claims to cover.
The mechanism is per runner, not one shape forced onto eight: python has a
last-sorted module, go a TestMain, ruby Minitest.after_run, java and kotlin
the end of main. Rust's libtest and Swift's XCTest have no after-all hook
that can fail, so there the manifest DRIVES the run — a required name with
no dispatch arm fails. sdks/README.md records the mapping.
This paragraph was once false: nothing read the file, and the coverage it
was created to hold could drift again unnoticed. It was, in two ports.
The last eighteen names cover the client-side write features (optimistic
layers, offline queue) rather than the wire. They assert against
fixtures/offline-optimistic.json, which carries the values and orderings
all eight ports must agree on.
`batch_entry_cap_matches_protocol` is the odd one out: it exercises no
behaviour, it pins a CONSTANT. The batch entry cap is normative and was
written out as a bare 500 in ten places with nothing reconciling them, so
each port now reads `offlineQueue.batchReplay.maxEntries` out of the
fixture and compares its own. Lower the server's cap without that and
every client keeps chunking at the old one, taking the coded 400 that
README 4.3 defines as terminal — durable writes discarded, not retried.
The ten names after it pin behaviour eight ports each got some of wrong on
their own: one replay-failure predicate for the single-call and batch paths,
a 413 split whatever the reply's shape, a committed-but-undecodable result
settled rather than retried or lost, a poke applied whole or not at all, a
frame handler that cannot be made to raise, an RPC that fails with the SDK's
own error type, streams that end on close, a session evicted on an identity
change, and a bearer token that never reaches a printed value.
The last name holds a write refused for its credential until a fresh token
is set, then replays it under that token (fixtures/offline-optimistic.json
`credentialRefresh`). Every port had the hold; the one that flushes on its
own when its socket connects did not flush when a new token landed, so the
held write waited for a reconnect that a healthy socket never makes.
A name here is required of EVERY port, so it may only assert behaviour
every port has. Where one legitimately differs the difference belongs in
the capability matrix, not here.
